questions.prompt:
Selwick Freight's Dynamics 365 Contact Center voice numbers use Azure Communication Services Direct Routing on a customer-managed session border controller (SBC). The SBC's fully qualified domain name is sbc1.selwickfreight.example, and its public certificate names only that domain.

Selwick is adding a Teams Direct Routing trunk to the same SBC and will move its numbers to that trunk in groups over several weeks. Numbers that haven't moved must stay in service on Azure Communication Services Direct Routing, and planned downtime isn't allowed on any line. At the end of the migration, Azure Communication Services Direct Routing is retired and Teams Direct Routing becomes the only path.

You need to plan the SBC transition so that it meets these requirements.

What should you choose for each planning item?
questions.answer: Domain name: use a separate domain name or alias for the Teams trunk. Certificate: use a certificate that covers both names, or separate certificates. Trunk removal: after validation confirms that no workload depends on it.
questions.explanation: Selwick needs one SBC to serve two platforms at once, which is the coexistence approach. An SBC fully qualified domain name can't be assigned to Azure Communication Services and Teams Direct Routing at the same time, so the Teams trunk gets a different name or alias. The SBC certificate must then cover both names, or separate certificates are used. A full cutover would reuse the same name, but it can cause downtime and would remove the numbers that haven't moved from the trunk they still need. The old configuration is removed only after post-cutover validation confirms that the migration is stable and that no workload depends on it.

optionExplanations.r1a: Fails. An SBC fully qualified domain name can't be assigned to both services at the same time.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. Moving the name is the full cutover approach. It can cause downtime, and numbers that haven't moved must stay on Azure Communication Services Direct Routing.
optionExplanations.r1c: Correct. The coexistence approach configures a different fully qualified domain name or alias for the Teams trunk.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. For coexistence, the SBC certificate must cover both domain names, or separate certificates are used.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. The current certificate names only sbc1.selwickfreight.example, so it doesn't cover the new domain name.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. The public certificate must come from an accepted certificate authority.
optionExplanations.r3a: Fails. Syncing a number doesn't show that the migration is stable or that nothing still depends on the old configuration.
optionExplanations.r3b: Correct. Microsoft says to confirm that the migration is stable and that no workload depends on the previous configuration before removing old routes.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. Removing the SBC before carrier routing changes belongs to a full cutover that reuses the same domain name. With coexistence, the old trunk stays until validation is complete.

questions.prompt:
External phone number transfer is turned on for the Collections and Outage voice channels.

You need to configure the external transfers so that they meet the business requirements.

What should you configure for each item?
questions.answer: Collections: clear Use bridged transfers. Outage: select Use bridged transfers. SBC: accept REFER-TO for sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com, convert it to an INVITE and send it back to that host.
questions.explanation: Use bridged transfers changes who sees which number and whether capture continues. With it cleared, a new call begins: the external party sees the customer's number, the customer's keypad input reaches the external number, and recording and transcription stop. That fits every Collections requirement. With it selected, the original call continues: the external party sees the Dynamics phone number, and recording and transcription continue. That fits the Outage requirements. Collections is on Direct Routing, so clearing the setting also means that the SBC must accept the REFER-TO, convert it to an INVITE and send it back to complete the transfer.

optionExplanations.r1a: Fails. A bridged transfer shows the Dynamics phone number as the caller ID and keeps recording and transcription running, so the fraud screening and no-capture requirements both fail.
optionExplanations.r1b: Correct. A new call begins, the provider sees the customer's number, the customer's keypad input reaches the provider, and recording and transcription stop.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. Secure settings can stop capture on a bridged transfer, but the call is still bridged, so the provider sees the Dynamics phone number instead of the customer's number.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. The original call continues, the line crew sees the Dynamics phone number, and recording and transcription continue.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. Without bridged transfers the external line sees the customer's number, and recording and transcription stop.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. Start setting controls whether capture starts automatically when a call begins. It doesn't carry capture onto the new call that an unbridged transfer creates.
optionExplanations.r3a: Fails. Clearing the setting already passes the customer's number as the caller ID. The documented SBC change concerns how the transfer request is handled.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. Microsoft says that Direct Routing customers who don't use bridged transfers must configure the SBC for this transfer.
optionExplanations.r3c: Correct. Direct Routing customers without bridged transfers must configure the SBC to accept this REFER-TO, convert it to an INVITE and send it back to sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com.

questions.prompt:
Voicemail is an overflow action on the Billing, Collections and commercial queues, and the account managers have inbound profiles.

You need to make sure that voicemails reach the people named in the business requirements.

Which action should you use for each group of voicemails?
questions.answer: Account manager voicemails: add the users to the default individual voicemail queue. Billing Back Office voicemails: add the users to the default group voicemail queue. Commercial Desk voicemails: route them to a dedicated voicemail queue by using an Organization phone number rule.
questions.explanation: Voicemails are split by how they were created. A missed direct inward call becomes an individual voicemail, and the representative must be in the default individual voicemail queue before the system can assign it to them. A queue overflow creates a group voicemail. It goes to the default group voicemail queue, which has no representatives until the triage team is added, and which needs no extra queues or rules. Every voice queue's voicemails arrive there, so separating commercial voicemails needs more routing: a voicemail queue for that team, and rules that use Organization phone number as the condition. That target can't be a voice queue, because voicemails are categorized as records.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for Commercial Desk. A voicemail recorded on an organization number can be routed on the Organization phone number condition, and more elaborate routing uses voicemail queues that you configure.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. The default voice queue handles voice calls. Voicemails are records, and they use the voicemail workstreams and queues.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for account managers. Representatives must be in the default individual voicemail queue for the system to assign their voicemails.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Voicemails can't be routed to voice queues, and Microsoft advises against sentiment-based rules for this routing.
optionExplanations.e: Correct for Billing Back Office. Queue overflow voicemails go to the default group voicemail queue, which has no representatives by default and needs no extra queues or rules.

questions.prompt:
The team is working through the voice agent issues in Copilot Studio.

You need to resolve Issue 1, Issue 2 and Issue 3.

Which configuration should you use for each issue?
questions.answer: Issue 1: turn off barge-in for the message. Issue 2: add an explicit action to the On Error topic. Issue 3: configure latency messaging.
questions.explanation: Each issue has its own cause. In Issue 1, barge-in lets callers interrupt a message by speech or keypad, and Microsoft lists compliance messages that shouldn't be interrupted as a reason to turn it off. In Issue 2, a message on its own isn't enough error handling for a real-time agent: the On Error topic needs an explicit action, such as a transfer or an end-call step, or callers can be left in silence. In Issue 3, latency messaging covers background operations that take longer than expected by playing a message or music.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for Issue 3. Latency messaging plays a message or music when background operations take longer than expected.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. This setting improves speech recognition. None of these issues is caused by the agent misunderstanding what a caller says.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for Issue 1. Barge-in covers keypad and voice interruptions, and Microsoft recommends turning it off for a compliance message that shouldn't be interrupted.
optionExplanations.d: Correct for Issue 2. The On Error topic handles orchestration errors, and Microsoft says that it needs an explicit action, such as a transfer or end call, because a message alone isn't sufficient.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. Speech sensitivity decides when a caller's turn has ended. It doesn't stop key presses, handle orchestration failures or fill a pause during a lookup.

questions.answer: Create a voice queue for each language and add the matching CSRs. Add route-to-queue rules that use Conversation.CustomerLanguage.

questions.prompt:
You are finalizing the routing design for the Billing and Outage workstreams.

You need to meet the routing requirements.

Which routing option should you use for each item?
questions.answer: Corvane: percentage-based allocation. Medical-priority customers: rule-specific overflow. Storm Desk: fallback queue.
questions.explanation: Each requirement applies at a different point in routing. Percentage-based allocation splits matched work across queues, including vendor queues, and it can include up to five queues that total 100 percent. Rule-specific overflow overrides a queue's overflow action for the work items that match one route-to-queue rule, which is how one group of callers gets different treatment while the others keep the queue's action. A fallback queue catches work that matches no rule. The default choice is the out-of-the-box queue for the channel type, so Storm Desk must be set as the fallback queue.

optionExplanations.a: Fails. Queue priority orders work across queues for representatives who belong to more than one queue. It doesn't choose the queue that a call is routed to.
optionExplanations.b: Correct for Corvane. Percentage-based allocation distributes work across queues, and Microsoft describes its use across contact center vendors.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for medical-priority customers. It lets one route-to-queue rule use its own overflow action, while other callers keep the queue's action.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. A condition set on the queue applies to every caller routed to that queue, so it can't treat medical-priority customers differently, and it can't act on a call that reached no queue.
optionExplanations.e: Correct for Storm Desk. If no rule matches, the work item goes to the workstream's fallback queue.

questions.prompt:
Orchard Lane Grocers runs Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone. On the Sentiment analysis page, Monitor real-time customer sentiment is set to Yes, and Send notifications when a customer's sentiment decreases to or below is set to Negative.

During a conversation in the Deliveries queue, the customer's sentiment decreases to Very negative. At that moment, the supervisors are in these states:
- Dara: Available, assigned to the Deliveries queue
- Emil: Busy, assigned to the Deliveries queue
- Ines: Away, assigned to the Deliveries queue
- Priya: Available, assigned to the Deliveries queue
- Tomas: Available, not assigned to any queue

You need to identify the supervisors who won't receive a notification.

Which two supervisors should you identify? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.answer: Ines and Tomas.
questions.explanation: The threshold sets the sentiment level that raises a notification, and Very negative is below Negative, so this conversation reaches it. Two further conditions decide who can receive it: a supervisor receives threshold alerts only when their presence is Available or Busy and they're assigned to a queue. Ines is Away, so she fails the first condition. Tomas is Available but isn't assigned to any queue, so he fails the second. Busy is an accepted presence here, so being occupied doesn't rule out Emil.

Trigger event: Representative Non-Response Time
Action: Move active conversation to waiting
Action: Send a message
Action: Release conversation back to queue for reassignment

optionExplanations.a: Correct, and part of the solution. This trigger measures how long a customer stays inactive after the representative's last message.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. This trigger measures how long a representative leaves a customer's message unanswered, which is the opposite situation.
optionExplanations.c: Correct, and part of the solution. For asynchronous channels, this action moves the conversation to Waiting, and the representative is notified when the customer restarts it.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. This action sends a message and leaves the conversation in Active, where the representative's capacity is still consumed.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. This action reassigns the conversation to a different representative in the same queue, so it's no longer this representative's conversation when the customer replies.

questions.prompt:
Pinecrest Logistics runs a custom messaging channel through Messaging APIs in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. The channel instance is on a messaging workstream, and its queue often has a backlog.

While customers wait, they must get a message with their current place in the queue every five minutes until a representative is assigned.

You need to configure the message.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
questions.answer: Add a custom message for the Estimate Wait Time Notification trigger with {QueuePosition} in the text, and set Message interval to 5 minutes with isRecurring turned on.
questions.explanation: Messaging API channel instances have their own wait time notification. It's a custom automated message on the Estimate Wait Time Notification trigger, and the {QueuePosition} variable shows the customer's current place. Message interval sets how often it's sent, and isRecurring repeats it until a representative is assigned. The other routes look similar, but they can't meet the five-minute cycle. The Customer wait time setting sends updates on fixed intervals of 30 or 60 seconds, and the average wait time messages apply to live chat and voice. The {$...$} format is for context variables, so with no such variable it becomes an empty string.

options.text: On the channel instance, add a custom message for the Estimate Wait Time Notification trigger, and include {QueuePosition} in the text.
In the custom message pane, set Message interval to 5 minutes, and turn on the isRecurring toggle.
On the Behaviors page of the channel instance, turn on Customer wait time, and select the option to show customers their position in the queue.
On the Automated messages page, activate the Average wait time for customers: Minutes message for the channel.
On the channel instance, add a custom message for the Customer's position in queue trigger, and include {$QueuePosition$} in the text.

optionExplanations.a: Correct, and part of the solution. This is the trigger for Messaging API channel instances, and {QueuePosition} shows the customer's current position.
optionExplanations.b: Correct, and part of the solution. Message interval sets the time between messages, and isRecurring repeats the message until a representative is assigned.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Queue position notifications from this setting go at fixed intervals of 30 or 60 seconds, so it can't send one every five minutes.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. The average wait time messages apply to live chat and voice channels only, and they give a wait time and not a place in the queue.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. {$...$} is the context variable format, and a variable that isn't found becomes an empty string. Message interval and isRecurring are documented for the Estimate Wait Time Notification trigger.

questions.prompt:
Sorrel Lodge Hotels runs Dynamics 365 Contact Center standalone. Its booking portal has a chat widget that uses authenticated chat with a JSON Web Token (JWT). Proactive chat is turned on, and after lcw:ready the page calls startProactiveChat when a signed-in guest has spent 30 seconds on a booking.

The developer based the page on Microsoft's proactive chat samples, which call setContextProvider to send values. The booking reference and loyalty tier are sent this way, but they don't reach the conversation, although the workstream has context variables with the same names. The portal's token service already knows both values.

You need to send both values so that they can be used for routing and shown to the representative.

What should you do?
questions.answer: Add both values to the lwicontexts claim in the JWT payload.
questions.explanation: The samples for proactive chat use setContextProvider, but Microsoft notes that this method works for unauthenticated chat only. For authenticated chat, context travels in the JWT. The lwicontexts value in the payload holds serialized custom context, its keys must correspond to the workstream's context variables, and the values can be used for routing or shown to the representative. The widget's sign-in state decides the method, and proactive chat doesn't change that.

options.text: Add both values to the lwicontexts claim in the JWT payload.
Add both values to the JWT header beside the alg and typ values.
Call setContextProvider before the lcw:ready event is raised.
Set isDisplayable to true for both values in setContextProvider.
Add both values to the notificationUIConfig object for the invitation.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. Pass lwicontexts in the JWT payload for authenticated chat. Its keys must match the workstream's context variables, and it can carry values for routing or display.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. The JWT header holds values such as alg, typ and kid. Context variables go in the lwicontexts claim of the payload.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. SDK methods run after lcw:ready, and setContextProvider isn't supported for authenticated chat at any point.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. isDisplayable controls display of values that setContextProvider passes, and that method isn't supported for authenticated chat.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. notificationUIConfig customizes the invitation, including its message. It doesn't set context variables.

questions.prompt:
Mossgrove Foods uses a survey from Customer feedback as the post-conversation survey on live chat in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. The survey agent is published in Copilot Studio, and the survey is selected on the channel with Powered by Microsoft Copilot Studio.

A maker changed the rating question so that it stores the 1 to 5 score in a new variable named MCS_Rating. Responses appear in the Customer feedback survey response table, but the satisfaction scores for conversations don't appear in the Omnichannel historical analytics report.

You need the scores to appear in the report.

What should you do?
questions.answer: Store the score as a numeric value in the MCS_CSAT variable.
questions.explanation: Two variable rules are at work. An added question's response is stored in Dataverse when its variable name starts with MCS_, which is why MCS_Rating appears in the response table. The report is more specific: scores for conversations appear in the Omnichannel historical analytics report if they're stored as numeric values in the MCS_CSAT variable. So the data was saved, but not in the variable that the report reads.

options.text: Store the score as a numeric value in the MCS_CSAT variable.
Pass the score in mcs_additionalcontext as a JSON key value pair.
Store the score as a text value in the MCS_CSAT variable.
Move the MCS_Rating question to a system topic other than Conversation Start.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. Microsoft says scores for conversations appear in the Omnichannel historical analytics report if they're stored as numeric values in MCS_CSAT.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. mcs_additionalcontext passes extra context to the survey agent. It isn't where the report reads scores.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Microsoft says scores for conversations appear in the Omnichannel historical analytics report if they're stored as numeric values in MCS_CSAT. A text value doesn't meet that condition.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Conversation Start is the only system topic to edit. Microsoft says all other system topics are disabled and must not be used.

questions.prompt:
Brightwell Insurance has a French-language chat widget on its Quebec workstream in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. The compliance team approved a set of French quick replies. Each one has the French locale and is associated with the Quebec workstream. French is enabled in the environment.

When the Quebec representatives open quick replies, they're offered the English replies, and they have to choose French in the View all pane to find the approved text.

You need these representatives to be offered the French replies without that extra step.

What should you do?
questions.answer: Change the language in each representative's personal settings to French.
questions.explanation: Three things decide which quick replies a representative sees: the language mapped to the channel instance, the language in the representative's personal settings, and the workstream. The widget language and the workstream are already right. The remaining factor is the representative's own setting, because when it's configured, it determines the language in which quick replies are available. Tags and workstream associations change which replies can be found, not the language that's offered.

options.text: Change the language in each representative's personal settings to French.
Remove the Quebec workstream association from the French quick replies.
Set Default input language to French in the Real Time Translation Settings.
Add a French tag to the approved quick replies.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. When a representative has a language configured, that setting determines the language in which quick replies are available.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. With no association, a reply is available to all representatives, but the language setting still decides which language they're offered.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Default input language is the language that translation uses for representatives. It doesn't decide which quick replies are offered.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Tags group quick replies, and finding replies by tag is still an extra step for the representative.

exhibits.title: Background
exhibits.body:
Marram Bay Utilities supplies electricity and water to about 410,000 homes and small businesses along Canada's Atlantic coast. A provincial regulator audits how outage calls are handled, and the company must serve customers in English and French.

Customer care has 190 customer service representatives (CSRs) at sites in Port Ansel and Cape Harlow, and 14 commercial account managers in regional offices. An outsourced partner, Corvane Contact Services, supplies extra CSRs for billing calls. Storm season runs from October to March, and outage calls can rise tenfold within an hour.

Marram Bay is replacing a ten-year-old on-premises call center platform with Dynamics 365 Contact Center in standalone mode. CSRs work in Copilot Service workspace. The program has these phases:
- Phase 1 moves the Outage line and the commercial numbers from the legacy platform to Dynamics 365 Contact Center before storm season.
- Phase 2 follows next spring. It moves the Billing and Collections lines, which already run on Dynamics 365 Contact Center, to their long-term telephony platform.

exhibits.title: Current environment
exhibits.body:
Telephony
- All numbers come from one carrier over SIP trunks to a customer-managed session border controller (SBC). The SBC's fully qualified domain name is sbc1.marrambay.example, and its public certificate names only that domain.
- The Billing and Collections numbers reach Dynamics 365 Contact Center through Azure Communication Services Direct Routing, using sbc1.marrambay.example.
- The Outage number, the commercial main number and the account managers' personal numbers still terminate on the legacy platform.

Routing
- Voice workstreams exist for Billing, Collections, Outage and Commercial. Channel operating hours is turned off on all of them.
- The Billing queue is open Monday to Saturday, 07:00 to 20:00. Its overflow conditions Out of operation hours and Work item limit exceeds both use the Voicemail action.
- Queues use out-of-the-box assignment methods. Skill-based routing isn't in use.

AI agents
- Billing Assistant is a Real-time voice agent on the Billing workstream. It uses GPT-Realtime, with English as its primary language and French as a secondary language. It asks each caller to choose a language. The Billing voice channel has the same languages.
- Outage Reporter is a Basic voice agent with classic orchestration on the Outage workstream. Staff are piloting it on an internal test number. Its first message is the regulator's safety notice, followed by a menu that callers can answer by speech or keypad.

Environments
- Marram Bay has development, test and production environments. Configuration is authored in an unmanaged solution in development.
- Conversation orchestration and consumption-based billing are set up in all environments. No playbooks are published. A wait-time priority playbook for the outage queues is in development.

exhibits.title: Business requirements
exhibits.body:
Collections card payments
A CSR transfers a customer who wants to pay by card to the automated line of Marram Bay's payment provider, which is an external number. The CSR leaves the call. The customer enters the card details on the phone keypad. The provider's fraud screening needs the customer's own number as the caller ID. Marram Bay must not record or transcribe this part of the call.

Outage escalations
For dangerous conditions, a CSR transfers the caller to the on-call line of a contracted line crew, which is an external number. That line accepts only calls that show a Marram Bay number. The regulator requires recording and transcription to continue after the transfer.

Voicemail
- A missed call to an account manager's personal number must become a voicemail assigned to that manager.
- Voicemails left when the Billing or Collections queues overflow must be triaged by the Billing Back Office team, with no additional queues or routing rules to maintain.
- Voicemails left on the commercial main number must go to the Commercial Desk team, not to Billing Back Office.

Routing
- Corvane must handle 30 percent of Billing calls in its own queue.
- When the Billing queue is over its work item limit, customers on the medical-priority register must be transferred to the Priority Care queue. Other callers keep the voicemail offer.
- English-speaking and French-speaking CSRs are separate teams with separate service-level targets. Each published line keeps one phone number.
- An outage call that matches no route-to-queue rule must go to the Storm Desk queue, not to the default voice queue.

exhibits.title: Technical requirements
exhibits.body:
- Keep the current carrier contract and the customer-managed SBC. Every number must end up on Teams Phone extensibility with Teams Direct Routing.
- The Outage and commercial numbers use a new Teams Direct Routing trunk in Phase 1.
- Billing and Collections must stay in service on Azure Communication Services Direct Routing throughout Phase 1. Planned downtime isn't allowed on any line.
- Author configuration in development. Use managed solutions wherever the documented migration procedure supports them.
- Production records must not be edited directly, and production must not be overwritten by an environment copy.

exhibits.title: Issues
exhibits.body:
Issue 1: During the Outage Reporter pilot, staff who know the menu press a key during the safety notice and skip it. The notice must always play in full.

Issue 2: When Billing Assistant has an orchestration failure, callers hear an apology and then nothing else happens. A failure must always lead to a definite next step.

Issue 3: Billing Assistant balance lookups can take several seconds. Callers hear nothing during that time, and some hang up.

Issue 4: All Billing Assistant escalations go to the single Billing queue, so French-speaking callers often reach CSRs who speak only English.

Issue 5: Callers who arrive after 20:00 and ask for a CSR are offered voicemail as intended. Callers who are still waiting in the Billing queue at 20:00 stay on hold after it closes.

groups.title: Bramwell Pet Insurance: claim call assignment

exhibits.title: Scenario
exhibits.body:
Bramwell Pet Insurance takes claim calls in a Dynamics 365 Contact Center voice queue named Claims Voice. The queue uses the least active assignment method and has no custom prioritization rules. Two user groups, Claims Specialists and General Service, are associated with the queue. Conversation orchestration is available in the environment, and no playbooks are published yet.

Bramwell has these requirements:
- Each call must be offered to claims specialists first.
- If no specialist has taken a call after 60 seconds, general service CSRs must also become eligible, and specialists must stay ahead of them.
- Every call must stay in Claims Voice so that the queue's service-level reporting isn't split.

You need to implement the assignment behavior.

exhibits.title: Background
exhibits.body:
Wrenfield Eyewear sells prescription glasses and contact lenses online to customers in the United States, Canada and Mexico. It has no stores and no phone line. Customers order on the website, upload a prescription and talk to Wrenfield by web chat or WhatsApp.

Customer care has about 120 customer service representatives (CSRs) in Denver and Monterrey, 24 licensed opticians who work part-time shifts, and 11 supervisors. Three of the supervisors are dispensing team leads, who also review prescriptions. A staffing agency supplies extra CSRs for the busy weeks before benefit plans reset in January.

Wrenfield moved to Dynamics 365 Contact Center in standalone mode last year. CSRs and opticians work in Copilot Service workspace. The Clear View program is now fixing problems from the first year and adding what the launch left out.

exhibits.title: Current environment
exhibits.body:
Web chat
All three chat widgets are live chat today.
- Shop Chat is on the public store. Visitors aren't signed in, and the widget has no chat authentication setting. Frame Finder, a Copilot Studio agent, answers first and escalates to the Orders queue. Reconnect to previous chat is off.
- Account Chat is on the My Account pages. Customers are signed in, and the widget uses a chat authentication setting. Reconnect to previous chat is off.
- Lens Consult is on the signed-in prescription pages and belongs to the Prescription Chat workstream. It uses a chat authentication setting. Reconnect to previous chat is on with a time limit, and its Redirect URL is blank.

WhatsApp and SMS
- WhatsApp runs through Twilio on one production business number, on the WhatsApp Orders workstream. The Contact Book is on. No AI agent runs on this workstream.
- WhatsApp Orders has two route-to-queue rules. Customer phone numbers that start with +52 go to the Pedidos queue, and numbers that start with +1 go to the Orders queue.
- A Power Automate flow named Loyalty Match runs when a WhatsApp conversation starts. It finds the contact by phone number and writes the customer's loyalty tier to the conversation.
- The Lab Delay template was created in the Twilio Content Template Builder, and WhatsApp approved it last week. It hasn't been added in Dynamics 365. A Power Automate flow named Lab Delay Notice is built, but its OutboundConfigurationId variable has no value yet.
- SMS also runs through Twilio. Contact lens reorder reminders use an SMS message template and an outbound configuration.

Queues
- The Orders, Pedidos and Returns queues use the Least active assignment method.
- The Prescription queue uses Highest capacity, and its workstream uses Exact Match on a Dispensing skill. The queue's operating hours are 07:00 to 21:00 every day.
- Each optician's shifts are set up as work hours on their bookable resource calendar. Wrenfield doesn't use shift bookings, and shift-based routing is off.

Workspace
- Prescription Chat uses a custom session template named Prescription Session and the out-of-the-box notification templates.
- Its preconversation survey asks for Lens type, with the answers Single vision and Progressive.
- Two scripts are associated with Prescription Session: Single Vision Check and Progressive Check. Neither is a default, so opticians choose one by hand.
- LensLab Tracker is the lab supplier's website. It allows iframe hosting.

Experience profiles
- Supervisor Desk has rank 1 and is mapped to the Omnichannel supervisor role.
- Prescription Care has rank 2 and is mapped to a custom role named Dispensing Reviewer. Its inbox is off.
- Frontline Messaging has no rank or roles. Current frontline CSRs were added to it by name. Its inbox is on with only the preconfigured views, and All active channels is on.
- Returns Pilot is new and has no rank, roles or users.
- No custom profile is set as the default.
- Frontline and agency CSRs hold the Omnichannel agent role. Opticians hold that role and Dispensing Reviewer. Dispensing team leads hold those two roles and Omnichannel supervisor.

Supervision and quality
- Supervisor Monitor, Supervisor Assign, Supervisor Transfer and Force Close are all set to Yes. Supervisors work from the Ongoing conversation report.
- Block capacity for wrap up is set to Always block on every messaging workstream.
- Quality evaluation is set up for conversations. Chat Standards and Dispensing Standards are two separate published evaluation criteria, and all their questions are AI-enabled.
- Two evaluation plans are active. Store Review covers the Orders and Returns queues, and Prescription Review covers the Prescription queue. Both use Chat Standards, the Closed conversations trigger and the AI agent method.

exhibits.title: Business requirements
exhibits.body:
Requirement 1: Lens lab questions can take days. Account Chat customers must be able to leave, come back to the same conversation and its history, and send messages outside CSR hours. A CSR's capacity must not stay tied up while the customer is away.

Requirement 2: When a lens lab reports a delay, each affected customer must automatically receive the Lab Delay notice on WhatsApp, even if they haven't messaged Wrenfield for weeks. Customers opt in to WhatsApp updates at checkout.

Requirement 3: LensLab Tracker must open automatically in every Prescription Chat session, in a tab that opticians can't close.

Requirement 4: Before they accept a Prescription Chat conversation, opticians must be able to see the customer's language and lens type.

Requirement 5: Opticians must start on the script that matches the customer's lens type, and they must still be able to switch to the other script.

Requirement 6: Eight agency CSRs named by the Returns manager must use Returns Pilot for a six-week trial. They aren't in any custom profile yet. Wrenfield won't create a security role for a six-week trial, and the trial must not change anyone else's experience.

Requirement 7: A CSR who is working in the inbox must see new text conversations arrive there. A CSR or optician who is working anywhere else must get a session tab straight away, so that a new conversation isn't missed.

Requirement 8: Frontline CSRs need a view in their inbox that lists only the WhatsApp conversations that are unassigned in their queues. The view must appear for all of them without any action on their part.

Requirement 9: From next month, Prescription queue conversations must be evaluated against Dispensing Standards. Store Review must keep evaluating against Chat Standards, and the questions in Chat Standards must not change.

Requirement 10: An auditor needs every closed Prescription queue conversation from June evaluated one time. This must not leave an ongoing schedule behind.

exhibits.title: Technical requirements
exhibits.body:
- Stay on Dynamics 365 Contact Center in standalone mode. No voice channel is planned.
- The public store won't get a sign-in, so Shop Chat visitors stay anonymous.
- Keep WhatsApp and SMS on Twilio. Wrenfield must keep the ability to identify WhatsApp customers by phone number.
- The Prescription queue must stay open from 07:00 to 21:00. At least one optician is on shift throughout those hours, but shifts differ from person to person.
- Apart from time-limited trials, experience profiles must follow people's roles or apply to everyone. Administrators won't maintain lists of named users.

exhibits.title: Issues
exhibits.body:
Issue 1: Shop Chat visitors on phones often leave the chat to find or photograph a prescription, which can take 5 to 10 minutes. When they come back, they start again with a different CSR. They usually tell the CSR before they leave. They must be able to return to the same CSR.

Issue 2: Lens Consult customers who come back after the reconnection time limit are offered a new chat and join the queue again. They must be taken to the Book a Consultation page instead.

Issue 3: Some WhatsApp customers have adopted usernames, so only their Business-Scoped User ID reaches Dynamics 365. Their conversations reach neither the Orders queue nor the Pedidos queue, and their loyalty tier stays blank.

Issue 4: Opticians stay signed in and Available after their shift to finish lab paperwork. Prescription Chat conversations are still assigned to them during that time, while colleagues on shift have free capacity.

Issue 5: Dispensing team leads receive Supervisor Desk, but they need Prescription Care. All other supervisors must keep Supervisor Desk.

Issue 6: New users receive an out-of-the-box experience profile until an administrator adds them to Frontline Messaging. Every user who doesn't qualify for a role-mapped profile must receive Frontline Messaging, whichever roles they hold.

Issue 7: After each weekend, the Ongoing conversation report shows WhatsApp conversations in the Orders queue in the Open state. A supervisor must give specific ones to a senior CSR who is a member of that queue.

Issue 8: A CSR in the Orders queue has been called away. Her WhatsApp conversations are in the Active state, and they must go to another CSR in that queue.

Issue 9: A CSR left for the day with finished conversations in the Wrap-up state. A supervisor must close them now so that her capacity is free when she starts her next shift.

groups.title: Ashlake Campgrounds: handbook answers in Copilot

exhibits.title: Scenario
exhibits.body:
Ashlake Campgrounds runs 38 campgrounds across the US Midwest. It uses Dynamics 365 Contact Center in standalone mode, and its environment is in the North America region. CSRs answer chats in Copilot Service workspace, in English.

Site rules, pet rules and cancellation terms are in the Camp Rules Handbook, a set of PDF files in a SharePoint Online library. The library isn't on the public web. All CSRs have Read permission on it, and Restricted SharePoint Search isn't in use.

Copilot is enabled, and Copilot help pane - Ask a Question is selected in Copilot settings. The CSRs' experience profile has Ask a question turned on. Knowledge management is configured, but the knowledge base doesn't contain the handbook content. A Microsoft Copilot Studio license is available, and Ashlake accepts production-ready preview features.

Goal: A CSR must be able to type a question in Ask a question in the Copilot help pane and get an answer that's based on the handbook content.

You need to meet the goal.
